events.title: Columbus Sights the Americas
events.description: After more than two months at sea, Christopher Columbus and his Spanish-sponsored expedition made landfall in the Bahamas, at an island the Indigenous Lucayan people called Guanahani. Columbus renamed it San Salvador.
events.significance: This landfall opened lasting contact between Europe and the Americas. It set in motion colonization, global trade and profound upheaval for Indigenous peoples.

events.title: First Oktoberfest Celebrated in Munich
events.description: Bavarian Crown Prince Ludwig married Princess Therese of Saxe-Hildburghausen. The citizens of Munich were invited to celebrate the royal wedding with festivities on the fields outside the city gates, which were later named the Theresienwiese.
events.significance: The celebration grew into Oktoberfest, now one of the world's largest folk festivals. It draws millions of visitors to Munich each year.

events.title: Edith Cavell Executed
events.description: British nurse Edith Cavell was shot by a German firing squad in occupied Brussels during World War I. She had helped Allied soldiers escape to neutral territory.
events.significance: Her death caused international outrage and made her a symbol of courage and selflessness. She is remembered for her statement that patriotism is not enough.

events.title: Equatorial Guinea Gains Independence
events.description: Equatorial Guinea became independent from Spain, ending its period as a Spanish colony in West Central Africa.
events.significance: The country became one of Africa's newly sovereign states. Its independence is still marked as a national holiday.
